decisions.executionNote: Begin smooth elbow-up approach: vehicles to white, watches to blue, cameras to red. Raise and pitch both grippers before descending; object depths are visual estimates.
Approach the left bus and rightmost camera from above, maintaining separate workspaces. Keep grippers open while checking final alignment.
Correct depth and lateral alignment from wrist views; turn jaws across the bus and camera rather than along their lengths.
Lower with small visual centering corrections, then close on the bus and right camera. A short lift will test retention.
Lift both objects clear of the tabletop, then begin moving inward and forward over their assigned baskets while keeping grips closed.
Both objects remain visible in the closed jaws. Center over white and red baskets, then lower slightly for controlled release.
Guard stopped the forward motion. Replan from measured poses: lower first to regain joint margin, then make smaller centering corrections over the baskets; maintain closed grips.
Open both grippers over the assigned baskets and allow release, then retract backward and upward before approaching the next vehicle and camera.
Bus and first camera appear released into white and red. Approach the turquoise car with the left arm and the nearer central camera with the right, rotating jaws across each object's width.
Use wrist views to center the car and camera between the jaws while descending slowly. Depth remains uncertain, so retain open grippers for this approach.
Finish a short descent, close around the car and central camera, then lift vertically to check retention visually.
Lift the retained car and camera clear, then transport toward white and red baskets without crossing arms. Keep height moderate to avoid the previous reach guard.
Move the car and camera over clear areas inside their respective baskets while gradually lowering to release height.
The objects appear blocked by the front basket rims. Lift and retreat slightly, then tilt the tools forward to clear the rims without forcing the interrupted path.
No motion executed in the rejected chunk. First bridge the observed orientation toward the last accepted orientation, then lift away from the rim with small increments.
Advance slowly with the objects lifted above the rims and tools tilted forward. Keep both held until their centers are clearly over the basket interiors.
Lower slightly over the interiors, release the car and camera, wait for them to drop, then withdraw clear of the basket rims.
Both released objects are visible in their baskets. Approach the left watch and the remaining central camera, keeping each arm on its own side and pitching toward a top-down grasp.
Center the watch and last camera using wrist views, descending in small increments with open jaws. Check alignment again before closing.
Make the final small descent and camera lateral correction, close on the watch and camera, then lift slightly to test retention from RGB.
Lift to verify the watch and camera are retained, then start toward blue and red. Tilt tools forward gradually to clear rims without pushing the elbows toward their limits.
Watch and camera remain in the jaws after lifting. Carry them above blue and red, adding a little clearance and forward tilt before release.
Lower a little over basket interiors, release the first watch and last camera, allow them to settle, then retract. One watch remains on the right side of the table.
The first watch and all three cameras are visible in their assigned baskets. Withdraw the left arm toward home while the right approaches the remaining watch with jaws rotating across its band.
Finish aligning the right jaws across the watch and descend cautiously. Continue a smooth left-arm retreat toward its original pose.
Center the remaining watch, descend a final centimeter, close and lift to test retention. Finish returning the left arm to its initial pose.
Lift the last watch clear and carry it toward the right half of the blue basket, keeping the left arm parked and the right grip closed.
The last watch remains retained. Advance above the blue basket with a little additional forward tilt, keeping its drop location on the right side away from the first watch.
Lower the last watch slightly inside blue, open the gripper and allow it to settle, then withdraw backward and upward clear of the rim.
Both watches are visible inside blue; vehicles and cameras are in their separate baskets. Return the empty right arm toward origin with a smooth backward retreat and wrist leveling.
Continue returning the right arm toward its original pose with the gripper open; all sorted objects appear settled in their baskets.
